Citigroup (NYSE:C) has received regulatory approval to establish a wholly owned securities company in China, Citigroup Securities (China) Company Limited.

The new unit is set to offer equities brokerage, securities underwriting, and research services to onshore and international clients.

This approval expands Citigroup's onshore footprint in China's capital markets through a dedicated securities entity.

The new Citigroup Securities China approval is important, but it is only one part of the broader Citigroup story. Check out 5 other big wins that Citigroup investors should know about.

Citigroup operates as a global banking group that provides financing, trading, and advisory services to a wide range of corporate, government, and institutional clients. As a result, a deeper foothold inside China's securities market plugs directly into its core role in cross-border capital flows.

Does the team leading Citigroup have what it takes? See our full breakdown of the management team's track record and compensation.

Why does this new China securities license matter for Citigroup's strategy?

The onshore license lets Citigroup move from being mostly an offshore arranger around China to running equities brokerage, underwriting and research inside the country. That plugs directly into its global services and cross border payments network, which already targets corporate and institutional clients that raise capital and trade in multiple markets.

How does this approval connect to Citigroup's current funding moves in the bond market?

Recent fixed income offerings, ranging from 5.30% notes due 2028 to 6.70% notes due 2046, expand Citigroup's pool of senior unsecured funding across several maturities. That kind of term financing can support investments in onshore platforms like Citigroup Securities China while the bank continues to manage capital returns and regulatory requirements.

Does this change the Citigroup Narrative investors have been using?

The license lines up with the existing Narrative that focuses on global services growth, digital payments and AI supported productivity rather than replacing it. It adds another way to use that services and technology stack in a large market, while the same regulatory and conduct risks highlighted in the Narrative still need close attention.

title: Citi Says Adobe Could Be Headed for a Hard Reset
detail:
Citi Says Adobe Could Be Headed for a Hard Reset
Moz Farooque ACCA
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 12:53 PM MST 2 min read
ADBE
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Adobe (NASDAQ:ADBE) came under fresh pressure Wednesday after Citi downgraded the stock to Sell from Neutral and cut its price target to $207 from $250, warning that consensus expectations for fiscal 2027 may still be too high.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with META.

Is ADBE fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

ADBE GF Value chart

Citi sees a rising risk of what it called a hard reset as incoming CEO Anil Chakravarthy takes over on December 1 amid important leadership vacancies, including the CFO and head of Digital Media. The bank expects those changes, combined with a shifting Creative strategy, could lead to a weaker fiscal 2027 outlook when Adobe reports fourth-quarter results.

The strategic shift is important.

Adobe is increasingly prioritizing user growth through AI products such as Firefly rather than relying as heavily on Creative Cloud price increases. Citi believes that could help expand Adobe's funnel over time, but it may hurt annual recurring revenue growth in the near term as more users enter through lower-priced products.

The bank estimates that this strategy could create roughly 200 basis points of pressure on fiscal 2027 ARR growth, with another 50-basis-point headwind as Adobe laps previous Creative Cloud pricing increases. Citi also cited weak small-business demand and growing competition from web-based and AI-native creative tools.

As a result, Citi cut its net new ARR estimates for fiscal 2027 and 2028 by roughly $470 million and $500 million, respectively. It now expects total ARR growth of about 5.3% in fiscal 2027 and 4.5% in fiscal 2028, roughly 200 to 300 basis points below Wall Street expectations.

Margins could face pressure too.

Citi lowered its fiscal 2027 non-GAAP gross-margin estimate by 70 basis points, partly reflecting AI inference costs that Adobe has not yet fully monetized.

Investor Takeaway

I think Citi's call gets to the heart of Adobe's problem.

The company is not necessarily losing the AI race, but the economics of adapting to it may be worse before they get better.

Adobe wants more users, more Firefly adoption, and stronger positioning against AI-native rivals. But if that means fewer price increases, lower-priced entry products, and higher inference costs, near-term ARR growth and margins could weaken at exactly the wrong time.

That is what Citi means by a hard reset.

For investors, the key things to watch are Adobe's fiscal 2027 guidance, Creative ARR growth, Firefly monetization, pricing strategy, executive appointments, and whether AI-first user growth eventually converts into higher-value subscriptions.

Adobe still has enormous scale and a powerful installed base.

The question is whether Wall Street is still modeling the transition too generously.

title: TREE Plans First Share Buyback Since 2022: What's Driving the Move?
detail:
TREE Plans First Share Buyback Since 2022: What's Driving the Move?
Zacks Equity Research
Wed, November 4, 2026 at 10:28 AM MST 4 min read
TREE
BAC
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

LendingTree, Inc. TREE announced plans to resume share repurchases in the fourth quarter of 2026, marking its first buyback activity since the first quarter of 2022. The decision reflects management's confidence in the company's improving financial position and its belief that TREE shares are attractively valued.

The announcement follows LendingTree's voluntary repayment of $60 million in long-term debt in the third quarter of 2026. Management highlighted debt reduction and share repurchases as its preferred capital allocation priorities, ahead of acquisitions and other investments.

TREE's Improving Balance Sheet Supports Buyback Plans

LendingTree has made considerable progress in strengthening its balance sheet. At the end of September 2026, the company had approximately $336 million in gross debt and $83 million in cash, translating into net leverage of 1.7X, down from 2.6X a year ago and 3.5X in the fourth quarter of 2024.

LendingTree, Inc.

Image Source: LendingTree, Inc.

The company is also approaching its stated objective of reducing net debt to $200 million. Its trailing 12-month levered free cash flow, adjusted for one-time litigation payments, reached approximately $100 million by the end of September 2026, underscoring its improving cash-generation capabilities.
Cash provided by operating activities increased to $76.4 million in the first nine months of 2026 from $56.6 million in the year-ago period. Such improvements provide LendingTree with greater flexibility to reward shareholders while continuing to strengthen its financial position.

Strong Revenue Growth Provides Additional Support

LendingTree's revenues for the first nine months of 2026 increased 23.4% year over year to $984.3 million from $797.6 million. Insurance revenues totaled $666.1 million, supported by strong carrier demand and continued expansion across its partner network. Home revenues reached $124.5 million, benefiting from healthy home equity lending demand, while Consumer revenues totaled $193.8 million.

The variable marketing margin increased to $281.8 million in the first nine months, while adjusted EBITDA reached $116.8 million, reflecting continued earnings growth. However, elevated marketing expenses pressured profitability, with the variable marketing margin declining as a percentage of revenues.

For 2026, LendingTree expects revenues of $1.30-$1.31 billion, variable marketing margin of $370-$375 million and adjusted EBITDA of $151-$153 million, indicating continued business expansion and earnings growth.

Investing.com -- Citi upgraded infrastructure group Ferrovial NV to "buy" from "neutral" on Wednesday, saying the fall in its shares since it won the I-24 toll road concession does not reflect the project's underlying economics.

Citi set a target price of €59.40 per share, down from €59.50. Citi expects a total return of 16.8% over 12 months, made up of a 14.9% share price gain and a 1.9% dividend yield.

Ferrovial shares are -7% since the Aug. 19 award, versus -2% for the SXOP index.

At its worst, the company lost about €8.7 billion, or about 22%, of its market value, and has since recovered about €3 billion after disclosing the concession payment structure.

Citi said the market had feared the $24.8 billion concession fee would have to be paid upfront or over a compressed construction period, straining cash or forcing a share sale. The disclosures showed most of it is paid over the concession's life.

Citi estimates I-24 can generate a 13.2% internal rate of return on equity, assuming 75% debt and 25% equity funding with $5.4 billion of equity injected late in construction.

Ferrovial holds 65% of the project. A $1 billion change in construction cost would move that return by 50 basis points.

Citi expects earnings per share to grow about 13% a year over 2027-30, against a peer average of 5%, driven mainly by pricing power in its toll roads.

Revenue per transaction is up double-digit across the portfolio, even as traffic trends are mixed.

The operating U.S. managed lanes and the 407 ETR toll road in Canada make up 80% of Citi's equity valuation.

Citi raised its per-share earnings estimates 8% over 2026-28, citing more optimistic growth in construction and energy and a weaker euro against the U.S. and Canadian dollars. They are 3-9% ahead of analyst consensus over 2026-30.

Citi flagged upcoming events it expects to be positive: the commercial close of I-285E in December, the financial close of I-24 in July 2027, and a possible request for proposals on North Carolina's I-77 South by year-end, for which Ferrovial is shortlisted. Citi opened a positive 90-day catalyst watch on the stock.

Citi's bull-case price is €95 and its bear case is €40.

title: Citi Sells Clients on Bitcoin ETFs Despite $1 Billion Outflows
detail:
Citi Sells Clients on Bitcoin ETFs Despite $1 Billion Outflows
Lockridge Okoth
Tue, November 3, 2026 at 8:30 AM MST 2 min read
C
BTC-USD
SOSO-USD
ETH-USD
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citi is pitching spot Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs (exchange-traded funds) to its wealth clients. Over the last two trading sessions, investors pulled about $1 billion from US Bitcoin ETFs.

On Monday, US Bitcoin and Ethereum ETFs lost $538 million combined. These funds, which let investors own crypto through a brokerage account, held $111.3 billion that day, per SoSoValue.

What Citi's Crypto Report Tells Its Clients

Citi Wealth published "Expanding the Investable Universe: Introduction to Crypto ETFs" in October. It says suitable investors want new assets to sit beside their stocks and bonds.

The report cites regulatory clarity, institutional adoption, and low long-term correlation with traditional assets, meaning crypto has not tended to move in step with them. It also lists risks and suitability limits.

How Much Money Has Left the Funds?

US spot Bitcoin ETFs lost $398.62 million on November 2, SoSoValue data shows. Investors had pulled $643 million out on October 30, a day after hackers took $6.3 billion from Binance.

Spot Bitcoin ETF Flows. Source: SoSoVlaue

When investors redeem ETF shares, issuers sell or hand back the Bitcoin behind them. Withdrawals therefore add supply to the coin's market.

Ethereum ETFs shed $139.80 million on November 2, extending outflows seen in most sessions since early October.

Still, the latest Bitcoin outflow equals about 0.4% of the $98.12 billion the funds hold. BlackRock's IBIT alone lost $405.3 million in a day, BeInCrypto reported.

Why Citi's Bitcoin Custody Launch Has No Date

Citi said in August that its Custody+ platform will start safekeeping Bitcoin for institutions later this year.

By Sigel's count, that makes Citi the sixth of 29 global systemically important banks, the lenders regulators treat as too big to fail, with Bitcoin custody live or announced. JPMorgan has said custody is off the table for now, he added.

Sigel also offered an unconfirmed reason for the silence.

"The Binance hack last week could be one reason Citi has stayed quiet on timing. I heard that the service was already set for launch last week," he said.

Citi has not confirmed that account, and its public guidance remains "later this year." BeInCrypto first reported the Citi custody plans in August.

Whether Citi names a date before December 31, and whether ETF withdrawals ease, will show if Wall Street's build-out and investor demand line up again.

title: Apollo Taps European Private Credit Markets With New Lending Platform
detail:
Apollo Taps European Private Credit Markets With New Lending Platform
Zacks Equity Research

APO
GS
C
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Apollo Global Management, Inc. APO is expanding its private credit business with the launch of European Credit Company ("ECC"), a dedicated European lending platform with more than €10 billion ($11.2 billion) in lending capacity. Backed by Apollo funds and institutional investors, the platform will focus on performing corporate and asset-backed credit, strengthening APO's European lending capabilities.

How Will ECC Strengthen APO's European Lending Business?

The launch comes as demand for alternative financing gains momentum across Europe. As companies increasingly look beyond traditional banks for funding, private credit has emerged as an important source of capital. Rising institutional demand and the relatively low penetration of nonbank lending offer further room for market growth, creating opportunities for Apollo to expand its lending activities.

To capitalize on this opportunity, Apollo is building ECC as a dedicated pan-European origination and financing platform. It will provide financing across multiple credit asset classes, including corporate and asset-backed lending. ECC will target large and mid-market financing opportunities involving companies, financial sponsors and real asset owners, particularly in sectors such as infrastructure and real estate. The platform currently operates across Frankfurt, Jersey, London, Luxembourg City and Milan, with plans to expand into additional European markets in the upcoming quarters.

Beyond its presence in these markets, ECC will leverage multiple channels to expand its lending business. These include proprietary loan origination, partnerships with European financial institutions and access to Apollo's existing European credit platform. By combining these channels, ECC could strengthen local relationships, reach a broader pool of borrowers and generate additional lending opportunities across the region.

The launch also complements APO's broader efforts to expand its global private credit business and strengthen institutional relationships. In October 2026, the company announced a strategic investment to acquire a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, a move expected to deepen its Middle East relationships and broaden access to global alternative investment opportunities. Earlier, in September 2024, it partnered with Citigroup C to establish a $25-billion private credit and direct lending program. These initiatives, alongside ECC's launch, support Apollo's efforts to expand lending capabilities, strengthen origination networks and capture opportunities across international credit markets.

Meta Platforms Inc. is targeting at least $20 billion in a multi-currency investment-grade bond deal to gauge market appetite amid climbing skepticism over AI expenditures.

The company tapped Citigroup Inc. and Morgan Stanley to coordinate investor discussions for a transaction that will mark its first major debt issuance in six months and its maiden euro-denominated offering.

Maturity schedules for the potential issuance span five to 30 years for dollar-denominated notes and roughly four to 38 years for the euro tranche.

Meta Platforms (META) is exploring a substantial cross-border debt package of about $20 billion to fund its ongoing operations and capital needs, Bloomberg reported.

However, the report noted that final sizing has not been locked in and could expand based on active investor participation.

To kick off the process, the social media titan enlisted financial institutions Citigroup (C) and Morgan Stanley (MS) to lead investor discussions. The upcoming move follows a non-deal European roadshow held by the company last month, setting the stage for its first major debt transaction since April and its inaugural entry into the European bond market.

Surging AI Spending

The aggressive capital raise comes amid a broader wave of heavy borrowing by major technology firms. Over the past year, tech giants have rushed to raise hundreds of billions of dollars to construct data centers and buy advanced semiconductors. However, this heavy spending cycle has triggered anxiety regarding long-term financial returns.

Market unease is increasingly visible, with the cost of protecting prominent US technology debt against default reaching new peaks. Meta's proposed structure features dollar-denominated maturities ranging from five to 30 years, alongside euro notes stretching from just over four years to nearly 38 years.

Investor appetite for technology credit has visibly cooled since April when Meta previously tapped the high-grade market for $25 billion amid heavy demand, forcing issuers to offer sweeter terms. Peers like Alphabet Inc. (GOOG, GOOGL) and Oracle Corp.(ORCL) have recently had to offer elevated yields and new-issuance concessions to attract buyers for multi-billion-dollar deals.

Beyond debt markets, Meta has aggressively tapped equity channels to support its ambitious artificial intelligence roadmap. The company recently priced $25 billion in common stock, secured $12.5 billion through preferred shares, and outlined plans to pull in up to $60 billion via an at-the-market equity distribution program.
